name: Brisbane
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Brisbane: resources and infrastructure diligence, asset research and litigation support under Queensland law
hero_lede: Brisbane is Queensland's capital and the commercial centre for its resources, energy, agriculture and infrastructure sectors, with projects building toward the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, coordinating Queensland-licensed investigators and the client's Queensland counsel where local work is needed.
intro: Brisbane is the capital of Queensland and the centre of south-east Queensland, one of Australia's fastest-growing regions. The Australian Bureau of Statistics put Brisbane's population at 1.36 million in 2024, and Brisbane City Council reports a gross regional product of 225 billion Australian dollars in 2022-23. Health care, professional, scientific and technical services, and education are the largest employers, while the city also serves as the head office and service base for resources, energy, agribusiness and construction companies operating across Queensland. The Australia TradeCoast precinct around Brisbane Airport and the Port of Brisbane is a major employment and logistics district, and the city will host the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Brisbane because of the projects and capital that flow through it. Coal, gas and minerals ventures in regional Queensland are often financed, managed and litigated from Brisbane, and investors need to understand operators, contractors and joint venture partners. Large infrastructure and Games-related construction brings procurement and contractor integrity risk, and builder and developer insolvencies generate creditor claims. Property development and agricultural land attract domestic and foreign investment that calls for ownership checks. Litigators need witness, asset and corporate history research for proceedings in Brisbane's Supreme Court and Federal Court registries. Queensland's own licensing and listening device rules shape how fieldwork is done.

matters.title: Resources and energy partner diligence
matters.text: Coal, gas and critical minerals projects in Queensland are commonly managed from Brisbane through joint ventures and contractor networks. We research operators, partners, contractors and their principals for prior insolvencies, regulatory action, litigation and political exposure before investment, offtake or financing.

matters.title: Infrastructure and Games procurement integrity
matters.text: Transport, venue and urban projects linked to the 2032 Games involve many contractors and subcontractors. We help bidders, financiers and project owners assess ownership, phoenix company history, prior disputes and conflicts of interest among counterparties, so that integrity concerns surface before contract award.

matters.title: Construction insolvency and creditor recovery
matters.text: Builder and developer failures in Queensland leave subcontractors, financiers and purchasers pursuing recovery. We trace directors' related companies, property holdings and asset transfers before collapse, giving liquidators and creditors' counsel a sourced basis for claims and recovery decisions.

matters.title: Property and agricultural land ownership
matters.text: Investors acquiring Brisbane property or Queensland farmland, and lenders taking security, need to understand vendors and existing interests. We combine Queensland land title searches with company records and court history to identify the people behind ownership structures and any disputes affecting the asset.

matters.title: Litigation and witness research
matters.text: Commercial disputes heard in Brisbane often depend on witnesses and counterparties spread across regional Queensland, interstate and overseas. We locate witnesses, research backgrounds and reconstruct corporate histories for counsel, ensuring any fieldwork is done by Queensland-licensed investigators within state law.

local_context.title: Queensland investigator licensing
local_context.text: Private investigators working in Queensland must be licensed under the Security Providers Act 1993, with licences administered by the Office of Fair Trading. Licensees must renew before expiry and notify address changes within seven days. Since coercive control became a criminal offence in Queensland on 26 May 2025, it is an offence for a licensed investigator knowingly to facilitate domestic and family violence, and conviction brings ten years' licence disqualification.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Brisbane
local_context.text: The Supreme Court of Queensland, the District Court and the Magistrates Court sit in Brisbane, which is also the principal Queensland registry of the Federal Court of Australia. Large commercial, corporate and insolvency matters are commonly heard in the Supreme Court or the Federal Court, depending on the claim. Counsel selects the forum, and investigative research is shaped to its disclosure rules and any orders made.

local_context.title: Queensland privacy and recording rules
local_context.text: Queensland regulates the use of listening devices under its own legislation, which differs from New South Wales and Victoria in when a participant may record a private conversation and how recordings may be used. Commonwealth privacy law, described on the Australia page, applies alongside it. Any recording, surveillance or tracking in Brisbane is therefore planned with Queensland counsel and carried out only by licensed investigators.

local_context.title: Land titles and company records
local_context.text: Queensland land is registered under the Torrens system, and title searches through the Queensland Titles Registry identify registered owners, mortgages and other dealings. Companies are registered nationally with ASIC, so Brisbane-based companies appear in the federal register rather than a state register. Linking title, ASIC and court records is usually needed to identify who stands behind property holdings and related lending.

local_context.title: Growth and the 2032 Games
local_context.text: South-east Queensland has grown at about 1.8 percent a year over recent years, and the region expects substantial job growth before 2032. The Olympic and Paralympic Games are driving major venue, transport and urban development spending. Rapid growth and large public programmes historically increase exposure to contractor failure, procurement disputes and fraud, which is why integrity diligence on project counterparties is relevant in Brisbane now.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Brisbane and handles Brisbane matters from Nashville. We first confirm with the client and its Queensland counsel the purpose of the work, whether a resources investment, a project procurement, an insolvency recovery, Supreme or Federal Court litigation or an internal review, because that determines what may be collected and how. Research draws on ASIC company records, Queensland land titles, court judgments and listings, regulatory decisions and local media, and extends into other states and countries where counterparties operate. Surveillance, witness enquiries and other fieldwork are carried out by investigators licensed under Queensland's Security Providers Act 1993. Reports cite sources and are prepared for use by counsel.

faqs.q: Do investigators in Brisbane need a Queensland licence?
faqs.a: Yes. Private investigators working in Queensland must hold a licence under the Security Providers Act 1993, administered by the Office of Fair Trading. A licence from another state or country does not authorise work in Brisbane. TDSC coordinates Queensland-licensed investigators for fieldwork and plans the work with the client's Queensland counsel.

faqs.q: Can TDSC help vet contractors on Games-related projects?
faqs.a: Yes. We research contractor and subcontractor ownership, directors' prior companies and insolvencies, litigation, regulatory action and media coverage. The aim is to identify phoenix activity, undisclosed related parties and conflicts of interest before contracts are awarded or financed. Findings are sourced so procurement and compliance teams can act on them.

faqs.q: How do you trace assets of a failed Queensland builder?
faqs.a: We map the directors' current and former companies through ASIC records, search Queensland land titles for property held personally or through related entities, and review court judgments and insolvency notices. We look for transfers shortly before collapse. Liquidators and creditors' counsel then decide whether to pursue voidable transaction or other recovery claims.

faqs.q: Which courts in Brisbane hear large commercial disputes?
faqs.a: The Supreme Court of Queensland and the Brisbane registry of the Federal Court of Australia hear most large commercial, corporate and insolvency disputes, with the District Court handling mid-value claims. The choice depends on the cause of action and the relief sought. We tailor research to the procedure of the chosen court.

faqs.q: Can conversations be recorded in Brisbane investigations?
faqs.a: Queensland has its own listening device law, which governs when a party to a private conversation may record it and how the recording may be used or communicated. The rules differ from other Australian states. We do not record conversations ourselves and plan any such step with Queensland counsel and licensed investigators.
